rationale: C04 plausibly supplied a material drafting template for the child. Both are proclamations establishing a new national monument under section 2 of the 1906 Act and use the same operative machinery: preservation of valid existing rights; immediate reservation of federally owned or controlled lands within described boundaries; automatic incorporation of nonfederal lands upon federal acquisition; withdrawal from appropriation under the public-land laws; a monument-administration provision; and the same warning against damage or settlement. C03 and C18 contain closely related acquisition and reservation language, but C04 is strongest because it likewise establishes a monument and combines that language with an express public-land withdrawal.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Section 2 of the Act of June 8, 1906 ... authorizes the President ... to declare by public proclamation ... objects of historic or scientific interest ... to be national monuments ... the limits of which ... shall be confined to the smallest area compatible with the proper care and management of the objects to be protected.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas, under section 2 of the act of June 8, 1906 ... the President is authorized "to declare by public proclamation ... objects of historic or scientific interest ... to be national monuments ... the limits of which ... shall be confined to the smallest area compatible with the proper care and management of the objects to be protected"
shared_material.explanation: The child closely tracks C04's statutory-authority recital and smallest-compatible-area formulation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: there are hereby set apart and reserved as the Noatak National Monument all lands ... and waters owned or controlled by the United States within the boundaries of the area depicted
shared_material.parent_excerpt: federally owned or controlled lands within the exterior boundaries of the following described area are hereby reserved from all forms of appropriation under the public land laws and set apart as the Marble Canyon National Monument
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same core establishment mechanism: described federal lands are reserved and set apart as a newly named national monument.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Lands ... and waters within these boundaries not owned by the United States shall be reserved as a part of the monument upon acquisition of title thereto by the United States.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: State-owned lands within those boundaries shall become and be reserved as parts of that monument upon acquisition of title thereto by the United States
shared_material.explanation: This is a concrete contingent-reservation provision, adapted in the child to encompass all nonfederal land, submerged land, and water.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The establishment of this monument is subject to valid existing rights
shared_material.explanation: The same savings condition qualifies the monument reservation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: All lands ... and all waters within the boundaries of this monument are hereby appropriated and withdrawn from entry, location, selection, sale or other disposition under the public land laws
shared_material.parent_excerpt: federally owned or controlled lands ... are hereby reserved from all forms of appropriation under the public land laws
shared_material.explanation: The child expands C04's public-land withdrawal machinery with a more detailed list of prohibited dispositions and an express water reservation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Warning is hereby given to all unauthorized persons not to appropriate, injure, destroy or remove any feature of this monument and not to locate or settle upon any of the lands thereof.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Warning is hereby expressly given to all unauthorized persons not to appropriate, injure, destroy, or remove any feature of this monument and not to locate or settle upon any of the lands thereof.
shared_material.explanation: The warning is nearly verbatim, reinforcing the broader operative correspondence, though it would not independently establish templating.
